clauses.reason: Executive Order 10319, signed 1952-01-04 (17 FR 188), recites a dispute between the Northwest Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, and under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its four operative sentences are: the creation sentence, with the rule that no member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction that the board report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date" of the order; the direction that "the board shall comply with the" requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence, which, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, bars any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the date of the order until thirty days after the board reports. The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. Later event: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 states that the parties returned to direct negotiations, which resulted in an agreement dated April 24, 1952, that no effort was made to name the board members, that the board "functioned until said agreement was reached", and that no report to the President was made. The board was therefore never constituted and never reported; the agreement of 1952-04-24 is recorded as a spent fact, and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 (report deadlines; a board never constituted) the order nevertheless stayed on the books until its express revocation. The three thirty-day extensions of reporting time named in the same record are disclosed without dates, because neither their dates nor any extension instrument is held; an extension of a deadline is not an end. The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 10 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "10319 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute", which agrees with the order's title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188, Federal Register of January 8, 1952; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 10319, signed by Harry S. Truman and dated January 4, 1952; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier listed seventeen clauses, but sixteen of them are fee-schedule paragraphs (spirits of turpentine, rosin, drums, tank cars) of a Department of Agriculture naval-stores rule printed on the same Federal Register page after the order. I replace them with one whole-order clause running from the heading to the sentence ending "dispute arose." The order has three recitals and four operative sentences: the creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act with the rule that no member be interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; the direction that the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The order does not mention any other Executive order or any officer other than the President. Later facts: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 (PEB-100-Report.pdf) states that the board members were never named because the parties returned to direct negotiations, that the President granted three thirty-day extensions of time, that the parties reached an agreement dated April 24, 1952, and that no report to the President was made. The agreement date is recorded here as a spent fact and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24; The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held.  the board was never constituted (owner rulings of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines and on a board never constituted). Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order. The held-text number-citation scan in the packet lookups found no other held text citing 10319.

savings.reason: EO 12553 attaches no savings or exception clause to its revocation list (its enacting provision is one sentence followed by the table). The board was never constituted and made no report; the dispute was settled by the parties' own agreement of April 24, 1952, which is not a command of this order. No continuing right or duty arising from the order is shown.
